h1: OMNI Hold Removal Lawyer El Paso, TX
intro: If the Texas Department of Public Safety refused to renew your driver's license, there is probably an OMNI hold from an unresolved ticket. Attorney Robert Navar tracks down every hold in every El Paso County court, resolves the cases behind them, and gets the clearances sent to DPS so you can renew.
summary: OMNI is the Failure to Appear program under Texas Transportation Code Chapter 706. When you miss a court date or leave a fine unpaid, the court reports you and DPS denies your license renewal until the court clears it.
Each court that reported you must send its own clearance, and each case carries a $10 OMNI fee. Holds from El Paso Municipal Court, the JP precincts and the area city courts are all separate.
Clearing a hold means resolving the ticket and any failure-to-appear charge behind it — we work for dismissal or deferred disposition so the hold comes off without a conviction.
Start with our free ticket and warrant lookup. We find every hold and every warrant and quote a flat fee before you pay anything.

sections.heading: What an OMNI Hold Is and Why DPS Won't Renew Your License
paragraphs: Transportation Code Chapter 706 lets Texas courts contract with DPS through a program most people know by its vendor name, OMNI. When you fail to appear on a citation or fail to pay a judgment, the court reports the case to the program. From that moment DPS flags your driver's license record, and the next time you try to renew — online, at the El Paso mega center on Hondo Pass, or anywhere else — the renewal is denied. You are told to contact the court.

The hold is not a suspension. You keep your current license until it expires. But once it expires you cannot renew, and driving on an expired license is how a simple OMNI hold turns into a no driver's license ticket or, after a formal suspension, a driving while license invalid charge. Many clients discover the hold only when a renewal is refused, years after the ticket.
Under the statute the hold stays in place until the court that reported it tells DPS the case has been resolved and the $10 OMNI fee for that case has been paid. No court clearance, no renewal.

sections.heading: Multiple Courts Mean Multiple Holds
paragraphs: This is where OMNI frustrates people. DPS does not resolve anything — it only checks whether every reporting court has cleared you. If you have an old EPPD ticket in El Paso Municipal Court, a Sheriff's citation in a Justice of the Peace precinct, and a stop in Socorro, you have three holds. Clearing one of them changes nothing at DPS until the other two are cleared too.

Each court also has its own paperwork, its own clerk's window and its own timing for transmitting the clearance. A client who pays off the Municipal Court case and walks to the DPS office the same afternoon is usually denied again, because the clearance has not posted and the JP case is still open.

Our first job is therefore to build the full list. We check every court in El Paso County — Municipal, each JP precinct, Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint, Anthony and Vinton — and report back what is open, which cases carry warrants, and what it will take to clear each one.

sections.heading: How We Find and Remove Every OMNI Hold
paragraphs: Fill out the free lookup form with your name and date of birth, or call 915-503-1600. Within a business day our office tells you every open case, the court it sits in, whether a warrant is attached, and a flat quote. There is no charge for the search.

Once hired, we file a notice of appearance on each case. Any warrants are recalled, usually within 24–48 hours in Municipal Court. Then we resolve the underlying tickets the way we resolve any citation — through dismissal or deferred disposition under Code of Criminal Procedure art. 45.051 — rather than by pleading guilty and paying the fine. That matters, because a hold cleared by a guilty plea leaves a conviction on your record; a hold cleared by dismissal or deferral does not.
When each case closes, we make sure the $10 OMNI fee is paid and ask the clerk to transmit the clearance to DPS. We then confirm the clearance posted before telling you to go renew.

sections.heading: What OMNI Hold Removal Costs
paragraphs: Our pricing is the same flat structure we use for every ticket: $59 per case in El Paso Municipal Court and $69 per case in JP, Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint and Anthony courts, with discounted add-on rates for extra citations from the same stop. If a warrant is attached, add $35 for the first warrant and $20 for each additional one. The court's own $10 OMNI fee per case, and any court costs tied to a deferral, are paid to the court.

Compare that with the alternative most people try first: paying every old fine in full. A driver with four aged tickets across two courts can easily owe $1,000 or more, and after paying it all they have four convictions reported to DPS and the insurance increases that follow. Clearing the same four cases through us typically costs a fraction of that and, in most cases, ends with no convictions at all.

sections.heading: Timeline: From Hold to Renewed License
paragraphs: Most OMNI matters in El Paso Municipal Court clear within a few weeks: a day or two to recall warrants, one pretrial setting to resolve the cases, and a few days for the clerk to transmit clearances. Deferred disposition adds the 90–180 day deferral period, but the hold itself is typically released when the deferral is granted, not when it ends, so you can renew while the deferral runs. Smaller courts move on their own docket schedules and may add a week or two.

If your license has already been suspended for a separate reason — points, a DWI, or an unresolved surcharge from before the 2019 repeal — clearing OMNI is necessary but not sufficient, and you may need an occupational driver's license to drive legally meanwhile. We handle both. Fort Bliss soldiers, UTEP students and clients who have moved out of state are all handled without a trip back to El Paso. Se habla español.

sections.heading: Don't Pay the Fines Online to Clear a Hold
paragraphs: Online payment portals make it easy to pay old tickets, and that is exactly the problem. Every payment is a guilty plea and a conviction on your DPS record. If the tickets were moving violations, those convictions carry points toward a suspension and are visible to your insurer for three years. Paying also may not clear a separate failure-to-appear case, leaving the hold in place after your money is gone.
Let us look first. The lookup is free, the quote is flat, and the outcome we work for is a clean record and a renewed license. This page is general information, not legal advice about your case.

faqs.q: How do I know if I have an OMNI hold?
faqs.a: DPS will deny your renewal and tell you to contact the court, but it will not always list every court. Our free lookup checks each court in El Paso County and reports every open case, hold and warrant.

Under Transportation Code Chapter 706, the court collects a $10 administrative fee for each case it reported to the Failure to Appear program. The fee must be paid before the court will send the clearance to DPS. It is per case, so three reported cases mean $30.

faqs.q: Can I just pay the tickets to remove the hold?
faqs.a: You can, but paying is a guilty plea that puts a conviction on your record for every ticket, with points and insurance consequences. We clear the same hold by resolving the cases through dismissal or deferred disposition so the hold comes off without the convictions.

faqs.q: How long does OMNI hold removal take?
faqs.a: In El Paso Municipal Court, usually a few weeks from hiring to a posted clearance. Warrants are typically recalled within 24–48 hours, the cases resolve at one pretrial setting, and the clerk transmits the clearance within days. Smaller courts can take a little longer.

faqs.q: I have holds from courts in other Texas cities. Can you help?
faqs.a: We handle every court in El Paso County. For holds from courts elsewhere in Texas, we will identify them in the lookup and tell you what each court needs, so you know the full picture before you start.

faqs.q: Is an OMNI hold the same as a license suspension?
faqs.a: No. A hold blocks renewal; a suspension takes away driving privileges now. If you have both, clearing the hold is the first step, and an occupational license may let you drive legally while the suspension runs.
